rubrics.justification: The response gives a plausible fair-quality blastocyst assessment and appropriately comments on expansion, ICM, and TE, but it is somewhat overconfident with specific localized features (e.g., upper-left ICM, granularity, perivitelline debris) that may not be clearly verifiable from a single image and broadens the grade to 3–4BB/4BC.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, BMI, first cycle status, sperm motility, and endometrial thickness, and connects them to prognosis, though a few points such as diet/stress are more speculative than central.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent, with prognosis tied to embryo quality and patient factors. Probability estimates are logically explained, though some numerical adjustments appear heuristic rather than rigorously derived.

Core recommendations such as SET in a young favorable-prognosis patient are guideline-consistent, but several adjuncts and future suggestions (ERA after one failure, endometrial scratch, aspirin/vitamin E/sildenafil/acupuncture) are not strongly guideline-supported or are presented too favorably.

The response provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support review, embryo inventory review, and possible male-factor follow-up, though some recommendations are more optional or weakly evidence-based.
